body_long:
Franck Chaumès has been elected confederal president of Umih, France's main employers' organisation for hotels, restaurants, cafés and nightlife, which says it represents more than 35,000 businesses in mainland France and overseas. He succeeds Thierry Marx. Valentin Prudon was elected confederal vice-president on the same ticket, representing the hotel side. Umih announced the result on 13 October 2026.

The vote was close. The duo was elected by a majority of departmental presidents and affiliated unions, by a margin of about 300 votes over Brice Sannac, president of Umih Pyrénées-Orientales.

## A restaurateur from Gironde

Franck Chaumès comes from four generations of restaurateurs. Since 1990 he has developed several businesses, notably in Bordeaux and around the Arcachon basin. He has presided over Umih Gironde since 2021 and has led the organisation's national restaurant branch since 2023.

He takes over from Thierry Marx, the two-Michelin-starred chef of Sur Mesure at the Mandarin Oriental, Paris, who led Umih for one four-year term from October 2022. Marx had himself succeeded Roland Héguy, who chaired the organisation for twelve years.

## The programme

The new leadership has set four priorities: giving Umih more weight in public decision-making; protecting the profitability of businesses facing regulatory pressure and unfair competition, including from platforms; defending both traditional restaurants and independent hotels; and giving departmental unions more resources and a bigger role in national action.

Several initiatives were announced: new member services offering legal, tax and social support backed by artificial intelligence; UmihLab, a lab designed to make innovation accessible to independent operators; a Sommet de l'Hospitalité française for professionals and decision-makers; and a Semaine de l'Hospitalité française open to the public.

## The signal

The hotel industry will watch two subjects closely: the balance between restaurants and hotels in the organisation's agenda, and its relationship with the other main employers' group, the GHR, which congratulated the new president while questioning the new direction. For hoteliers, the questions on the table are familiar: furnished holiday rentals, pricing freedom with booking platforms and the tourist tax.

Congratulations to Franck Chaumès and Valentin Prudon on their election.
summary: He succeeds Thierry Marx as confederal president of France's main hospitality trade union.
